Human: Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 7 repository files
- about 27 functions or methods
- about 617 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 6 and 8 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- workbook-like sheets rows and cells
- CSV import and export as a portable interchange
- column selection and filtering
- sorting and aggregation
- missing and invalid value handling
- deterministic processing reports

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 7 repository files
- about 27 functions or methods
- about 617 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 6 and 8 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- workbook-like sheets rows and cells
- CSV import and export as a portable interchange
- column selection and filtering
- sorting and aggregation
- missing and invalid value handling
- deterministic processing reports

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.\\n\\nPer-file concrete design and implementation tasks:\\n- CMakeLists.txt:\\n  - Define project with C++17 standard.\\n  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.\\n  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.\\n  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.\\n  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).\\n- include/ExcelCore.h:\\n  - Declare namespace excel with:\\n    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().\\n    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. {"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. {"filename":"src/ExcelCore.cpp","design_doc":{"root_path":"docs/system_design","filename":"20260913013307.json","content":"{\"Implementation approach\":\"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.\\n\\nPer-file concrete design and implementation tasks:\\n- CMakeLists.txt:\\n  - Define project with C++17 standard.\\n  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.\\n  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.\\n  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.\\n  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).\\n- include/ExcelCore.h:\\n  - Declare namespace excel with:\\n    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().\\n    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().\\n    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().\\n    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.\\n    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.\\n    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).\\n  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.\\n- src/ExcelCore.cpp:\\n  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).\\n  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.\\n  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.\\n  - Implement CSV parsing:\\n    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.\\n    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (\\\"\\\"), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.\\n    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.\\n    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).\\n  - Implement CSV export:\\n    - Write header if present in Sheet.\\n    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.\\n    - Emit platform-independent newlines (\\\"\\\\n\\\").\\n- include/ExcelOps.h:\\n  - Declare namespace excel with:\\n    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.\\n    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.\\n    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().\\n    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);\\n      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).\\n    - Filtering:\\n      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.\\n      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).\\n      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).\\n    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).\\n    - Aggregation:\\n      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.\\n      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).\\n  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.\\n- src/ExcelOps.cpp:\\n  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.\\n  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.\\n  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.\\n  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.\\n  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.\\n  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.\\n- src/Main.cpp:\\n  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.\\n- tests/test_main.cpp:\\n  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.\\n  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.\\n  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.\\n  - Keep total under 150 LOC, Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. column, ProcessingReport*).\\n  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.\\n- src/ExcelOps.cpp:\\n  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.\\n  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.\\n  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count metagpt.actions.add_requirement.UserRequ.content:
Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 7 repository files
- about 27 functions or methods
- about 617 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 6 and 8 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- workbook-like sheets rows and cells
- CSV import and export as a portable interchange
- column selection and filtering
- sorting and aggregation
- missing and invalid value handling
- deterministic processing reports

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.\\n  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare {"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

metagpt.actions.add_requirement.UserRequ.content:
Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 7 repository files
- about 27 functions or methods
- about 617 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 6 and 8 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- workbook-like sheets rows and cells
- CSV import and export as a portable interchange
- column selection and filtering
- sorting and aggregation
- missing and invalid value handling
- deterministic processing reports

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

metagpt.actions.add_requirement.UserRequ.content:
Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 7 repository files
- about 27 functions or methods
- about 617 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 6 and 8 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- workbook-like sheets rows and cells
- CSV import and export as a portable interchange
- column selection and filtering
- sorting and aggregation
- missing and invalid value handling
- deterministic processing reports

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly. Build a small, dependency-free C++17 project via CMake. Keep runtime entry thin and deterministic. Separate pure domain logic (workbook/sheet/cell, CSV parsing/serialization, filtering/sorting/aggregation, reporting) into reusable include/*.h + src/*.cpp modules. All I/O boundaries use std::istream/std::ostream so tests remain headless/offline. Tests include only headers. Provide a canonical API in two headers: ExcelCore.h (data model + CSV) and ExcelOps.h (operations + ProcessingReport). Use stable, deterministic rules for sorting, missing values, and invalid numeric parsing. Implement robust CSV parser with quoted fields and CRLF handling; exporter emits consistent quoting. Provide composable predicates and sorting specs. Aggregations (sum, count, average) ignore invalid/missing numeric cells, define behavior for empty sets deterministically.

Per-file concrete design and implementation tasks:
- CMakeLists.txt:
  - Define project with C++17 standard.
  - Add a core library target (excelcore) from src/ExcelCore.cpp and src/ExcelOps.cpp with PUBLIC include/ path.
  - Build an executable src/Main.cpp (excel_demo) linking excelcore.
  - Build a single test executable (excel_tests) from tests/test_main.cpp, link excelcore.
  - enable_testing() and add_test(NAME excel_tests COMMAND excel_tests).
- include/ExcelCore.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - struct Cell holding raw string; methods: isMissing(), asString(), parseInt(), parseDouble().
    - class Sheet managing headers, rows (vector<vector<Cell>>), name, and column name->index map. Methods: header access, hasColumn(), columnIndex(), appendRow(vector<string>), row/col counts, cell accessors, cloneWithSubsetColumns().
    - class Workbook storing named sheets; methods: addSheet(), sheetCount(), getSheetByIndex(), getSheetByName().
    - struct CSVConfig { delimiter, quote, hasHeader, trim }.
    - struct ImportResult { Sheet sheet; size_t rowsRead; size_t missingCells; }.
    - Functions: ImportResult importCSV(std::istream&, const CSVConfig&, const std::string& sheetName); void exportCSV(const Sheet&, std::ostream&, const CSVConfig&).
  - Include all needed standard headers: string, vector, unordered_map, functional, istream, ostream, optional, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelCore.cpp:
  - Implement Cell methods (missing detection, numeric parsing with whitespace trim and robust invalid detection).
  - Implement Sheet storage and manipulation: constructor(s) from headers, appendRow with size validation, name handling, column lookup with exceptions.
  - Implement Workbook store/retrieve by name/index with validation.
  - Implement CSV parsing:
    - Read lines with std::getline, strip trailing CR.
    - Parse fields respecting quotes, escaped quotes (""), delimiter inside quotes, and trimming if configured.
    - If hasHeader: first record as headers; else synthesize column names C1..Cn.
    - Build Sheet rows; track rowsRead and missingCells (empty fields after trim).
  - Implement CSV export:
    - Write header if present in Sheet.
    - Quote fields that contain delimiter, quote, newline, leading/trailing spaces. Escape quotes by doubling.
    - Emit platform-independent newlines ("\n").
- include/ExcelOps.h:
  - Declare namespace excel with:
    - enum class MissingOrder { First, Last }.
    - struct SortKey { std::string column; bool ascending; MissingOrder missing; } and struct SortSpec { std::vector<SortKey> keys; }.
    - struct ProcessingReport with counters (rows_read, rows_kept, rows_dropped, invalid_cells, missing_cells) and operations vector; methods addOperation(), merge(), toString().
    - Column selection: Sheet selectColumnsByNames(const Sheet&, const std::vector<std::string>&, ProcessingReport*);
      Sheet selectColumnsByIndices(const Sheet&, const std::vector<size_t>&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Filtering:
      - using RowPredicate = std::function<bool(const Sheet&, size_t)>.
      - Sheet filterRows(const Sheet&, const RowPredicate&, ProcessingReport*).
      - Helper predicate: RowPredicate makeNumericGreaterThan(const std::string& column, double threshold, ProcessingReport* reportForInvalidsOrNullptr).
    - Sorting: Sheet sortRows(const Sheet&, const SortSpec&, ProcessingReport*).
    - Aggregation:
      - struct AggregationResult { size_t count_valid, count_missing, count_invalid; double sum; std::optional<double> average; }.
      - AggregationResult aggregateNumeric(const Sheet&, const std::string& column, ProcessingReport*).
  - Include needed standard headers: string, vector, functional, optional, ostream, stdexcept.
- src/ExcelOps.cpp:
  - Implement ProcessingReport methods; deterministic toString() summarizing counts and operations in fixed order.
  - Implement selectColumnsByNames/Indices: validate names/indices, create new Sheet with subset columns, preserve order; update report with operation summary.
  - Implement filterRows: apply predicate for each row; build new Sheet preserving header; compute kept/dropped; update report; remain deterministic.
  - Implement makeNumericGreaterThan: resolve column index at first invocation via a captured lambda; parse double per row using Cell::parseDouble; treat missing as false; increment report->invalid_cells or report->missing_cells accordingly when provided.
  - Implement sortRows: stable_sort with comparator that evaluates keys in order; missing ordering policy explicit; when both numeric, compare numerically; else lexicographic compare; use stable_sort to ensure original order tie-breaking; update report with spec summary.
  - Implement aggregateNumeric: scan column, sum valid doubles, count missing/invalid; compute average only if count_valid>0; update report with a deterministic operation line.
- src/Main.cpp:
  - Demonstration: build CSV input via std::istringstream with headers and some missing/invalid numeric values; import with CSVConfig; compose ProcessingReport; filter rows where a numeric column > threshold using makeNumericGreaterThan; sort by a secondary column with missing last; aggregate numeric column; export to std::ostringstream; print a brief summary line and the report to std::cout; ensure program exits 0 without loops.
- tests/test_main.cpp:
  - Include only headers: include/ExcelCore.h and include/ExcelOps.h.
  - Test 1 (runtime wiring smoke): construct in-memory CSV, import, filter, sort, aggregate, export; assert row counts and that exported CSV contains expected header and row order.
  - Test 2 (core rule with missing/invalid): verify that filter predicate treats missing as false, invalid numeric increments report.invalid_cells, missing increments report.missing_cells, and aggregate ignores invalid/missing; check ProcessingReport toString() contains deterministic counts.

idea:
Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 7 repository files
- about 27 functions or methods
- about 617 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 6 and 8 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- workbook-like sheets rows and cells
- CSV import and export as a portable interchange
- column selection and filtering
- sorting and aggregation
- missing and invalid value handling
- deterministic processing reports

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents
